claims.text: A high-strength ceramic matrix composite containing an optimized fraction and dispersion of h-BN will provide stable self-lubrication over a wide temperature range while maintaining mechanical strength.
The initial material contains h-BN particles uniformly dispersed in a ceramic matrix at a baseline concentration.
Adjusting the proportion and dispersion of h-BN can optimize the chemical composition of the ceramic matrix composite.
The relevant structural mediator is the interfacial bonding and interaction between the ceramic matrix and h-BN particles.
Embedded h-BN particles form a lubricious tribofilm at elevated temperatures.
The ceramic matrix maintains the overall mechanical integrity of the composite.
The optimized composite will exhibit consistently low friction over a wide temperature range.
The optimized composite will exhibit reduced wear over a wide temperature range.
The optimized composite will retain mechanical strength under the proposed operating conditions.
The optimized composite will outperform non-optimized ceramics that lack lubrication or have diminished strength.
Current ceramic composites with non-optimized h-BN content or dispersion show either reduced high-temperature lubrication or compromised mechanical properties.
Exceeding a critical h-BN-content threshold may significantly diminish mechanical strength.
Nonuniform h-BN dispersion may prevent the expected tribological benefits from manifesting.
The optimum h-BN concentration and dispersion method may vary among ceramic matrices.
